correctness.rationale: In the basis 1,x,x²,(x−k_ε)_+², the four-node evaluation determinant is εLR(3εL+4εR+2L²+3LR)/4, nonzero for the entire stated positive-length regime. For p_ε=ε I_ε y, use the first difference quotient in place of the second nodal equation; the resulting system is polynomial in ε with a nonzero determinant at zero. Its inverse yields coefficient error O_{L,R}(ε||y||_∞). At the moving knot the polynomials match and their derivatives are uniformly bounded; comparing on the O(ε)-length moving knot and endpoint regions gives the same uniform error for the norms. The limiting operator is (y_2−y_1) times the derivative-one Hermite profile in the frozen proof. Its left positive peak is L(2L+3R)/(4(3L+4R)), greater than the right positive endpoint at the knot; the right trough has absolute size R²/(4(2L+3R)). Their difference has sign −(2r+1)(r²−2r−2), switching once at r=1+sqrt(3). Multiplying by the exact data factor 2 and dividing by ε gives the stated coefficient and the symmetric 5/(14ε) case. At equality both positions maximize the limiting profile; it is not asserted that both are exact norming locations at positive ε. The estimate is for fixed L,R, and merely opposite signs without saturation need not attain the factor 2; the data (−1,1,0,0) do. Independently checked the determinant, confluent solve, peak balance and equal-length coefficient in the truncated-power basis (python /workspace/branches/independent_math_checks.py, section 5).
